newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to introduce 10 pct duty on grains soon.
newsitem.headline: Poland to introduce 10 pct duty on grains soon.

text.p: The Polish government will soon introduce duties on most grain imports, which were originally scheduled to remain duty-free until the end of June, 1997, a government spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
Aleksandra Jakubowska told a news conference imports of durum wheat, maize and soybeans would remain duty free and the tariffs on other grains would be 10 percent.

"The Prime Minister (Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz) presented a proposal which has been approved by the government and which calls for the reinstatement of duties on grains...but it will not be a 20 percent duty but a 10 percent duty," she said.
Jakubowska said a necessary government regulation would be published within the next few days and would come into force 10 days after its publication in an official government bulletin.
Jakubowska added the 10-day grace period would allow firms to finalise contracts negotiated under previous regulations.
She also said the regulation included a clause that would allow duties to be suspended again if grain prices rose faster than overall consumer prices.
